messages:
maria: Heads up — customers and internal e2e are getting 401s hitting /v1/embeddings after today's RBAC rollout. Logs show: `error: missing scope: embeddings` :frowning:
kevin: Oof. Was the scope name changed in the policy migration? I thought we preserved `embeddings` vs `chat` scopes.
ashley: We renamed some scopes to `model:embeddings` and `model:chat` in the new policy to be per-model, but there was supposed to be a compatibility alias. looks like the alias didn't land.
sre-bot: Alert created: ENGSEC-437 — elevated 401 rate for embeddings endpoint (svc-auth error). link: https://internal/alerts/ENGSEC-437
maria: Quick repro for infra folks: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <legacy-token>" https://api.redwood.inf/v1/embeddings -> 401 / logs:
```
auth-service: token validation failed: scope check failed, required=\"embeddings\" granted=["generate","embeddings:legacy"]
```
kevin: The token shows `embeddings:legacy` which our new matcher doesn't accept. If KMS was rotated this morning that could also change signature verification, but logs show signature ok.
jordan: I pulled audit logs: tokens issued before 10:12 UTC (when migration ran) have the legacy label. The migration job deleted the compatibility map key due to a bad branch.
ashley: Proposed fast mitigation: re-enable alias mapping in auth-service to accept `embeddings:legacy` -> map to `model:embeddings` for 48h while we backfill tokens and publish SDK update. Less risky than rolling back the whole policy.
security-bot: Note: temporary aliasing must be logged and flagged for audit. Any temporary acceptance increases blast radius — we need an expiry TTL and a targeted allowlist (only internal and org-tier customers) :warning:
kevin: Agree. Implementation plan:
  1) Deploy auth-service patch that maps legacy scope names to new scope names with `temp_allow=true` and `expires_at` header.
  2) Add audit log entry `legacy_scope_mapped` with actor and original scope.
  3) Run targeted token re-issuer job for customers with active embedding usage.
ashley: I'll open the PR for the mapping in auth-service (assigning to kevin for review). PR will include log entries and a feature flag `compat/embeddings-scope`.
maria: I'll draft a customer-facing note for orgs showing they may see 401s and we're rolling a hotfix; want to avoid mass panic. Will include remediation: rotate keys if they observed other errors.
jordan: Also need to check KMS key versions: if a key rotation happened at 10:05, some tokens could be signed with v1 and verified with v2 — but current trace shows signature validation ok. I'll still run `kms list-key-versions` in staging and production.
kevin: Quick patch ready in branch `hotfix/legacy-scope-alias`. Unit tests added for `embeddings:legacy` -> `model:embeddings` and for `embeddings` raw.
ashley: Deploying patch to canary (us-west-2-canary) now. I'll flip the feature flag in canary only.
sre-bot: Deploy started: deploy-id=deploy-2026-03-20-1132 canary/us-west-2
maria: Any ETA for canary results? need to know if we should notify support to pause escalations.
kevin: Canary healthy after 4m. Canary logs show legacy tokens accepted and annotated with `legacy_scope_mapped: true`.
ashley: Rolling to prod with small bump and feature-flag on for org-tier only. Will monitor 15m then expand.
security-bot: Reminder: create a short-lived KMS key rotation rollback plan in case we see signature regressions when feature flag expands.
jordan: Running a quick audit query to count tokens granted `embeddings:legacy` in last 90d. Results: ~120 active tokens, top 5 tenants account for 80% of calls.
maria: I'll message support + account execs for top 5 tenants after prod confirmation.
kevin: Patch deployed to prod at 11:58 UTC with flag on for org-tier. Metrics: 401s for /embeddings dropped from 42/min -> 2/min (background test tokens). Rolling to all customers in 30m if stable.
sre-bot: Metric update: 401 rate decreased 95% in 10m window.
ashley: Expiry is set to 2026-04-03 in the mapping so we don't forget. We'll schedule a scheduled run to remove mapping unless the token reissue job completes.
security-bot: Post-incident actions required:
  - Full postmortem with timeline and root cause (who merged migration branch without alias key).
  - Add CI test to ensure compatibility mappings are present after migrations.
  - Update runbook: when RBAC migration runs, cross-check alias table exists.
maria: I'll own the postmortem doc and include remediation steps + SLA impact.
jordan: I'll run the token re-issuer for the top 5 tenants overnight and add a one-time notice in the console.
kevin: After this, we should add a unit check in migration runner: fail migration if alias table deletion detected.
maria: Thanks all — good quick work. After postmortem we'll plan a longer-term migration that includes a staged deprecation schedule, telemetry, and a documented KMS/key-rotation impact checklist. :thumbsup:
security-bot: Incident closed in tracker pending postmortem (ENGSEC-437).
